data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Ephrata means ‘fruitful’, derived from the root word meaning ‘fruit’. In the Bible, Ephrata is a place name and is also used as a feminine name. The name Ephrata carries the meaning “Fruitful” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ephrata usually hope their child will grow to embody fruitful and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: אפרתה
in_hebrew.meaning: עפרתה - פרי רוחני, שגשוג רוחני, או אדמת פריון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עפרתה היא שם עברי שמקורו בשורש פר"ה, שפירושו פרי או שגשוג. בהקשר רוחני, השם עפרתה מתאר את השגשוג והפרי הרוחניים המתפתחים בחייה של הנושאת את השם. הוא מוזכר בתנ"ך כמקום או ככינוי לאישה, ומשמעותו היא אדמת פריון או מקום של שגשוג רוחני.

in_greek.name: Εφρατα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Εφρατα στην ελληνική παράδοση προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή λέξη עפרתה (Ephratah), που σημαίνει καρπός ή ευφορία. Στην πνευματική έννοια, το όνομα Εφρατα συμβολίζει την πνευματική καρποφορία και την ευφορία που προκύπτει από την πνευματική ανάπτυξη και την εγγύτητα με το Θεό.

data.cultural_impact: Ephrata is most notably known as the location of the Ephrata Cloister, a historic site and National Historic Landmark in Pennsylvania, United States. Founded in 1732, the Ephrata Cloister was one of the earliest and most influential religious communities in America. The settlement was established by a German Pietist group known as the Sodalitia Asiatica, who believed in living a communal and ascetic lifestyle. Ephrata's impact can be seen through its contributions to American history, architecture, and art. The site features unique architecture, such as the Beehive House and the Savannah, both of which reflect the community's Celtic and Hebrew influences. The Ephrata Cloister is also known for its early American patient-care service, which provided medical assistance to the local community, as well as its music and art contributions, including the creation of some of the first hymnals and musical compositions in America.

In the Bible, the name Ephrata is associated with the Israelites and their journey to the Promised Land. In Genesis 48:16, Jacob blesses his son Joseph and says, "I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make of you a multitude of people." This spiritual significance of Ephrata is reflected in the Christian community's belief in bearing spiritual fruit through their actions, beliefs, and good works. The Ephrata Cloister community embodied this spiritual significance through their commitment to living a communal and ascetic lifestyle, caring for the sick, and creating music and art to praise and glorify God.

Joseph's other sons were Manasseh, Levi, and Benjamin. When Joseph died, his sons were given a double portion of land in Canaan, which was divided between the tribes of Manasseh and Ephraim. The name Ephrata is derived from the Hebrew word 'ephraim', meaning 'fruitful' or 'multiplying'.

The name 'Ephrata' was adopted due to Beissel's belief that he was fulfilling a prophecy from the Old Testament book of Judges, in which God promised to bless a place called 'Ephrata' with his presence.
